thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Recovery after distribution suspension: broken, as operating performance has continued to deteriorate with accelerating customer attrition [D03], [D07].
Management capability: broken, as the company explicitly acknowledges that centralizing service and dispatch damaged customer relationships with no leadership remedy in place [D03], [D07].
asks_if_escalating: Immediate board refresh to replace leadership responsible for failed service centralization
Operational audit to stem the 6.5% annual customer attrition rate
Strategic review of capital allocation given the suspended distribution and restricted cash from the propane disposal

drivers.driver: Accelerating annual customer attrition has reached 6.5%, up from 1.3% in fiscal 2003, signaling a failure in the core heating-oil franchise [D02], [D03].
Management's acknowledged failure to centralize service and dispatch has directly impaired customer retention and unit profitability [D03], [D07].
The suspension of the common distribution and the lack of a completed leadership remedy necessitate immediate, active intervention [D03], [D07].
Cash proceeds from the propane disposal are heavily restricted by debt-reduction covenants, limiting management's ability to pivot or return value without oversight [D02], [D04].

final.memo:
We are escalating our engagement with the Company. The thesis at purchase, which anticipated a recovery following the distribution suspension, has been severely compromised by management’s admitted failure to execute on service centralization, which has decimated customer relationships [D03], [D07]. Annual attrition has surged to 6.5%, a level that is fundamentally incompatible with a stable heating-oil distribution franchise [D02], [D03].

While the propane disposal provided a liquidity event, the proceeds are trapped by restrictive covenants and debt-reduction requirements, leaving common unitholders exposed to the ongoing decline of the remaining core business [D02], [D04]. The market is correctly wary of the company's prospects, as management offers no concrete remedy for the service-centralization issues or the resulting volume losses [D03], [D05].

We have seen enough. Management’s inability to stop the bleeding while the peak heating season progresses is unacceptable. We are going public to demand a board refresh and an immediate operational overhaul to protect our investment and ensure the remaining assets are managed for value rather than allowed to drift toward further erosion [D03], [D07].
